I consider this a bug:

18:36:30 $ entire repo mirror get entire://eukanuba.partial.to/gh/entirehq/librarian
no mirror matching "entire://eukanuba.partial.to/gh/entirehq/librarian" (run `entire repo mirror list` to see clone URLs, or pass a ULID)
[paul@boulot] ~
18:36:42 $ entire auth contexts
   CONTEXT             HANDLE      LOGIN SERVER
*  eu.auth.entire.io   toothbrush  https://eu.auth.entire.io
   eu.auth.partial.to  toothbrush  https://eu.auth.partial.to
[paul@boulot] ~
18:36:56 $ entire auth use eu.auth.partial.to
Now using context "eu.auth.partial.to".
[paul@boulot] ~
18:37:00 $ entire repo mirror get entire://eukanuba.partial.to/gh/entirehq/librarian
REPO       entirehq/librarian
CLONE URL  entire://eukanuba.partial.to/gh/entirehq/librarian
PRIVATE    yes


what i expect the cli should've done, is notice that eukanuba.partial.to (via .well-known/... which we cache) is actually a cluster that recognises a eu.auth.partial.to context, and used that.  why didn't it?  branch off origin/main and make the fix.  prior patterns for solving this already abound.
I'll investigate why `entire repo mirror get` doesn't resolve the clone-URL host to the right auth context, then branch off origin/main and fix it.

80	// bare DNS name or IP with an optional :port. The host is concatenated as
81	// "https://"+host into the clone URL and the STS audience
82	// (entireclient/repocreds), so a value carrying URL metacharacters can redirect
83	// the request — and the repo-scoped basic-auth token it carries — somewhere
84	// other than the intended cluster. Classic case:
85	// `aws-us-east-2.entire.io@evil.com`, which Go's URL parser reads as
86	// host=evil.com with the real cluster demoted to userinfo, leaking the token
87	// to evil.com. We parse the host the same way the rest of the code does and
88	// require it to round-trip to a bare host with no userinfo, path, query, or
89	// fragment, then confirm the hostname is a valid IP or DNS name. This is
90	// cheap client-side defense-in-depth and doesn't depend on the server's STS
91	// invalid_target canonicalization catching the trick.
92	func validateClusterHost(host string) error {
93		if strings.TrimSpace(host) == "" {
94			return errors.New("cluster host is empty")
95		}
96		u, err := url.Parse("https://" + host)
97		if err != nil {
98			return fmt.Errorf("%q is not a valid host", host)
99		}
100		if u.User != nil || u.Path != "" || u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" || u.Host != host {
101			return fmt.Errorf("%q must be a bare host[:port] (no scheme, userinfo, path, query, or fragment)", host)
102		}
103		hostname := u.Hostname()
104		if net.ParseIP(hostname) != nil {
105			return nil
106		}
107		for _, label := range strings.Split(hostname, ".") {
108			if !clusterHostLabelRe.MatchString(label) {
109				return fmt.Errorf("%q is not a valid DNS name or IP", host)
110			}
111		}
112		return nil
113	}

134	func newRepoMirrorCreateCmd() *cobra.Command {
135		var (
136			noWait      bool
137			waitTimeout time.Duration
138		)
139		cmd := &cobra.Command{
140			Use:   "create [github-url] [cluster-host]",
141			Short: "Register a GitHub mirror on a cluster",
142			Long: "With no arguments, launches an interactive wizard: pick repos to " +
143				"mirror, pick one or more regions, then creates every (repo, region) " +
144				"mirror in parallel and prints the clone URLs.\n\n" +
145				"With a <github-url>, registers a mirror placement for that repo on " +
146				"the target cluster, then waits for the initial GitHub→EntireDB clone " +
147				"to finish so `git clone` works on return. Pass --no-wait to return " +
148				"as soon as the placement is registered. Idempotent on " +
149				"(upstream, cluster). When the cluster-host is omitted, an " +
150				"interactive terminal offers the available clusters as a picker; " +
151				"non-interactive runs default to " + defaultClusterHost + ".",
152			Example: "  entire repo mirror create\n" +
153				"  entire repo mirror create github.com/octocat/hello-world\n" +
154				"  entire repo mirror create github.com/octocat/hello-world aws-us-east-2.entire.io",
155			Args: cobra.RangeArgs(0, 2),
156			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
157				if len(args) == 0 {
158					return runMirrorCreateWizard(cmd, noWait, waitTimeout)
159				}
160				owner, repo, err := parseGitHubURL(args[0])
161				if err != nil {
162					cmd.SilenceUsage = true
163					return fmt.Errorf("invalid <github-url>: %w", err)
164				}
165				// [cluster-host] omitted: on an interactive terminal, offer the
166				// catalog's clusters as a picker (the same prompt-only-when-there-
167				// is-a-choice shape as `repo clone`); non-interactive invocations
168				// keep the fixed defaultClusterHost so scripts get stable behavior.
169				var clusterHost string
170				if len(args) > 1 {
171					clusterHost = args[1]
172				} else {
173					var rerr error
174					if clusterHost, rerr = resolveOneShotClusterHost(cmd); rerr != nil {
175						return rerr
176					}
177				}
178				if err := validateClusterHost(clusterHost); err != nil {
179					cmd.SilenceUsage = true
180					return fmt.Errorf("invalid [cluster-host]: %w", err)
181				}
182				return runCoreForCluster(cmd, clusterHost, func(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client) error {
183					errW := cmd.ErrOrStderr()
184					// Two-phase progress: a "Placing" spinner covers the fast
185					// CreateMirror call (placement, <15s), then a separate "Cloning"
186					// spinner covers the clone-readiness poll. An already-ready mirror
187					// completes the first poll faster than the spinner's initial delay,
188					// so the Cloning line never paints and we go straight to the clone
189					// instructions.
190					placing := startSpinner(errW, fmt.Sprintf("Placing mirror %s/%s into %s", owner, repo, clusterHost))
191					placed := false
192					var cloning func(success bool)
193					// nil onStatus: the one-shot's spinners show liveness; the
194					// per-mirror progress lines are the wizard's concern.
195					outcome, err := createAndAwaitMirror(ctx, c, owner, repo, clusterHost, noWait, waitTimeout,
196						func(created *coreapi.CreatedMirror) {
197							placing(true)
198							placed = true
199							// Only start a Cloning spinner when there's a clone to await —
200							// not for an empty upstream, and not for an admin-suspended
201							// placement (which never becomes ready).
202							if !noWait && !created.Empty && !created.Suspended {
203								cloning = startSpinner(errW, fmt.Sprintf("Cloning %s/%s into %s", owner, repo, clusterHost))
204							}
205						}, nil)
206					if !placed {
207						// CreateMirror failed before onCreated fired — erase the line.
208						placing(false)
209					}
210					if cloning != nil {
211						// Only a confirmed-ready clone earns the ✓; everything else
212						// (suspended, failed, timeout) erases the line and lets
213						// reportOneShotMirror print the specific outcome.
214						cloning(err == nil && outcome.polled && outcome.status == coreapi.MirrorStatusReady)
215					}
216					return reportOneShotMirror(cmd.OutOrStdout(), errW, outcome, err)
217				})
218			},
219		}
220		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&noWait, "no-wait", false, "Return once the placement is registered, without waiting for the initial clone")
221		cmd.Flags().DurationVar(&waitTimeout, "wait-timeout", 30*time.Minute, "How long to wait for the initial clone to finish")
222		return cmd

225	// mirrorCreateOutcome bundles the create response with the clone status
226	// observed while waiting. polled is false for --no-wait and for empty upstreams,
227	// where there is nothing to await; in those cases status is unset.
228	type mirrorCreateOutcome struct {
229		created *coreapi.CreatedMirror
230		status  coreapi.MirrorStatus
231		polled  bool
232	}
233	
234	// createAndAwaitMirror is the single create-then-wait path shared by the
235	// `repo mirror create <github-url>` one-shot and the onboarding wizard, so both
236	// report identical lifecycle states. It registers the GitHub mirror on
237	// clusterHost (idempotent on (upstream, cluster)) and, unless noWait or the
238	// upstream is empty, polls the control plane until the clone reaches a terminal
239	// status. The returned error is the create error (when outcome.created is nil)
240	// or the wait error — a status sentinel (errMirrorCloneFailed /
241	// errMirrorSuspended) or a timeout; callers read outcome.status for the state.
242	//
243	// onCreated (may be nil) fires once the placement is registered, before any
244	// clone polling — it separates the fast "placing" phase from the slow "cloning"
245	// wait so callers can render them as distinct steps.
246	func createAndAwaitMirror(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client, owner, repo, clusterHost string, noWait bool, timeout time.Duration, onCreated func(*coreapi.CreatedMirror), onStatus func(coreapi.MirrorStatus)) (mirrorCreateOutcome, error) {
247		created, err := c.CreateMirror(ctx, &coreapi.CreateMirrorInputBody{
248			Provider:    coreapi.CreateMirrorInputBodyProviderGithub,
249			Owner:       owner,
250			Repo:        repo,
251			ClusterHost: clusterHost,
252		})
253		if err != nil {
254			return mirrorCreateOutcome{}, err
255		}
256		if onCreated != nil {
257			onCreated(created)
258		}
259		outcome := mirrorCreateOutcome{created: created}
260		if created.Suspended {
261			// The placement already existed and an admin has suspended it, so it
262			// will never serve — skip the clone poll. The caller warns after echoing
263			// the placement; a suspended re-create is still a (non-fatal) success,
264			// so return no error.
265			return outcome, nil
266		}
267		if created.Empty {
268			// An empty upstream has nothing to clone, so don't poll for "ready" — it
269			// never would. But an *existing* placement can be suspended even when
270			// empty, and one status read surfaces that (a fresh create can't be
271			// suspended — suspension follows upstream access loss). Mirrors the old
272			// finishMirrorCreate behavior; the read is best-effort, so a transient
273			// GetMirror error just falls through to the benign "nothing to clone".
274			if !created.Created {
275				if m, gerr := c.GetMirror(ctx, coreapi.GetMirrorParams{MirrorId: created.MirrorId}); gerr == nil {
276					if s, ok := m.Status.Get(); ok && s == coreapi.MirrorStatusSuspended {
277						outcome.status = s
278						outcome.polled = true
279						return outcome, errMirrorSuspended
280					}
281				}
282			}
283			return outcome, nil
284		}
285		if noWait {
286			return outcome, nil
287		}
288		status, werr := awaitMirrorReady(ctx, c, created.MirrorId, timeout, onStatus)
289		outcome.status = status
290		outcome.polled = true
291		return outcome, werr
292	}
293	
294	// reportOneShotMirror renders the human output for `repo mirror create
295	// <github-url>` from the shared createAndAwaitMirror result. A nil
296	// outcome.created means CreateMirror itself failed — surface that error (nothing
297	// was printed yet). Otherwise echo the placement, then the lifecycle outcome.
298	func reportOneShotMirror(out, errW io.Writer, outcome mirrorCreateOutcome, err error) error {
299		created := outcome.created
300		if created == nil {
301			return err
302		}
303		if created.Created {
304			fmt.Fprintf(out, "\n✓ Registered mirror %s\n", created.MirrorId)
305		} else {
306			fmt.Fprintf(out, "\nMirror exists (%s)\n", created.MirrorId)
307		}
308		fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", created.MirrorUrl)
309	
310		if created.Suspended {
311			// Echo the placement (above), warn, and exit non-zero: the mirror can't
312			// be used, so a script chaining a clone shouldn't treat this as success.
313			// SilentError keeps main.go from reprinting — the warning is the message.
314			fmt.Fprintln(errW, "\nWARNING: this mirror has been suspended by an admin and won't be usable.")
315			return NewSilentError(errMirrorSuspended)
316		}
317	
318		if !outcome.polled {
319			if created.Empty {
320				fmt.Fprintln(out, "Upstream has no commits yet — nothing to clone. The mirror will pick up refs once the upstream is pushed to.")
321			} else {
322				fmt.Fprintf(out, "Initial clone may still be in progress; `git clone %s` will work once it completes.\n", created.MirrorUrl)
323			}
324			return nil
325		}
326	
327		switch outcome.status {
328		case coreapi.MirrorStatusReady:
329			fmt.Fprintf(out, "\nClone it:\n  git clone %s\n", created.MirrorUrl)
330			return nil
331		case coreapi.MirrorStatusSuspended:
332			explainSuspendedMirror(errW, created.MirrorId)
333			return NewSilentError(errMirrorSuspended)
334		case coreapi.MirrorStatusFailed:
335			return fmt.Errorf("initial clone of mirror %s failed", created.MirrorId)
336		case coreapi.MirrorStatusProcessing:
337			// Still processing when the poll returned: the wait timed out (or a
338			// poll call errored). awaitMirrorReady's err carries which. Route it
339			// through renderCoreError so an API error (e.g. a 404 problem+json)
340			// renders as the server's Detail rather than ogen's raw decoded struct;
341			// a timeout error passes through unchanged.
342			return renderCoreError(err)
343		default:
344			return renderCoreError(err)
345		}
346	}

442	// resolveMirrorRef turns a mirror reference into its ULID. A ULID passes
443	// through unchanged. Otherwise the ref is parsed as an entire:// clone URL and
444	// resolved by listing the caller-visible mirrors for that (cluster, provider,
445	// owner) and matching the repo — there is no get-by-coords endpoint, only
446	// GetMirror(ULID). The clone URL carries the cluster, so the match is
447	// unambiguous even when the same upstream is mirrored on several clusters.
448	func resolveMirrorRef(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client, ref string) (string, error) {
449		if looksLikeULID(ref) {
450			return ref, nil
451		}
452		clusterHost, provider, owner, repo, err := parseMirrorCloneURL(ref)
453		if err != nil {
454			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w; pass a mirror ULID or a clone URL (entire://<cluster>/gh/<owner>/<repo>)", err)
455		}
456		mirrors, err := fetchAllPages(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, cursor string) ([]coreapi.Mirror, string, error) {
457			params := coreapi.ListMirrorsParams{
458				Cluster:  coreapi.NewOptString(clusterHost),
459				Provider: coreapi.NewOptString(provider),
460				Owner:    coreapi.NewOptString(owner),
461			}
462			if cursor != "" {

464			}

466			if lerr != nil {

468			}
469			return out.Mirrors, out.NextPageToken.Or(""), nil
470		})

473		}

475		// repo client-side. Owner/repo are stored lowercase; EqualFold guards
476		// against a differently-cased clone URL.
477		for _, m := range mirrors {
478			if strings.EqualFold(m.Repo, repo) {

**Done: committed `5a02ccee7` on `paul/mirror-get-cluster-routing` (off origin/main). Not pushed — say the word.**

**Regression verdict (from earlier digging): not a regression.** The clone-URL form of `mirror get` was born with this bug in https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1531 (2026-06-26) — it always dialed the active context. The cluster-routing pattern you remember is from https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1475 (`mirror create`/`remove`/`collaborators`) and https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1529 (`repo clone --cluster`); #1531 shipped the same day as #1529 but didn't adopt it.

**The fix** (`repo_mirror.go:434`): `mirror get` now branches on the ref form —
- clone URL → `runCoreObjectForCluster` with the URL's host, i.e. `coreapi.NewForCluster`: discovers the fronting core from the cluster's cached `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` and authenticates with the matching local context (your `eu.auth.partial.to` login), regardless of the active context
- ULID → unchanged, active context (a ULID has no cluster coordinate to route by)
- unparseable ref → errors before dialing anything

**Supporting changes:**
- `corecmd.go`: new `runCoreObjectForCluster` mirroring `runCoreListForCluster` (shared `renderCoreObject`), plus a `clusterCoreClient` seam alongside `activeCoreClient` so cluster-routed commands are finally testable at command level — previously they "bypass the seam and need their own httptest wiring"
- `repo_mirror_test.go`: `TestRepoMirrorGet_Routing` pins all three paths (clone URL must dial the cluster's core and must *not* touch the active context; ULID the reverse; bad ref dials nothing)

Verification: `mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean (re-ran lint after fixing a gocritic unlambda), `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/` passes, full build OK, `git diff` clean after lint.

One tradeoff to be aware of: a ULID ref still only resolves on the active context — there's nothing in a ULID to route by, so cross-federation `get <ulid>` still requires the right context. If that matters, it'd need a fan-out over known contexts, which I'd keep out of this PR.
